name: Find Pair
description: You've got another problem dealing with arrays. Let's consider an arbitrary sequence containing n (not necessarily different) integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . We are interested in all possible pairs of numbers ( a i , a j ), ( 1 ≤ i , j ≤ n ). In other words, let's consider all n 2 pairs of numbers, picked from the given array. For example, in sequence a = {3, 1, 5} are 9 pairs of numbers: (3, 3), (3, 1), (3, 5), (1, 3), (1, 1), (1, 5), (5, 3), (5, 1), (5, 5) . Let's sort all resulting pairs lexicographically by non-decreasing. Let us remind you that pair ( p 1 , q 1 ) is lexicographically less than pair ( p 2 , q 2 ) only if either p 1 < p 2 , or p 1 = p 2 and q 1 < q 2 . Then the sequence, mentioned above, will be sorted like that: (1, 1), (1, 3), (1, 5), (3, 1), (3, 3), (3, 5), (5, 1), (5, 3), (5, 5) Let's number all the pair in the sorted list from 1 to n 2 . Your task is formulated like this: you should find the k -th pair in the ordered list of all possible pairs of the array you've been given.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and k ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 , 1 ≤ k ≤ n 2 ). The second line contains the array containing n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n ( - 10 9 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ). The numbers in the array can coincide. All numbers are separated with spaces. Please do not use the %lld specificator to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use cin , cout , streams or the %I64d specificator instead.
output_specification: In the single line print two numbers — the sought k -th pair.
